findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "search" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "fetch" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: contact_publisher, weather, search · Private data: search_datasets, get_dataset, preview_dataset, catalogue_overview, contact_publisher, subsurface_at_location, get_subsurface_record, search_subsurface, search, fetch · Public sink: contact_publisher, train_punctuality, electricity_grid · Destructive: contact_publisher, search_subsurface, weather.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: contact_publisher, weather, search · Private data: search_datasets, get_dataset, preview_dataset, catalogue_overview, contact_publisher, subsurface_at_location, get_subsurface_record, search_subsurface, search, fetch · Public sink: contact_publisher, train_punctuality, electricity_grid · Destructive: contact_publisher, search_subsurface, weather

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "preview_dataset" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
